subject: Linguistics
title: Idioms
description: A fast breakdown of Idioms for builders.

hook.text: 'Spill the beans' has nothing to do with beans—it means to reveal a secret.

buildup.text: Idioms are fixed expressions whose meaning can't be predicted from their individual words.

discovery.text: They are stored in memory as whole units, like very long words with frozen structure.

twist.text: Some idioms are partially flexible—you can say 'the cat is out of the bag' in passive voice.

climax.text: Every language has idioms, and they rarely translate: French says 'tomber dans les pommes' for fainting.

punchline.text: Idioms break the rules—and every language has them.

quiz.question: Why can't idioms be translated word for word?
options: Their meaning doesn't come from individual words
